title: Create financial reports with accurate data and formatting
description: A report system that pulls every figure from your source of truth, formats it your way, and flags anything it can't trace before the report ships.

api.title: API (Application Programming Interface)
api.content: A way for two programs to talk to each other. When a tool says 'connect via API,' it means software can send requests and get data back automatically — no manual copy-paste needed.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

children.text: Every rebuild of a recurring report is a fresh chance for a number to arrive without a source. [Anthropic's guidance on reducing hallucinations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations) recommends the fix this system is built on. Cite a source for each claim, and retract anything unsupported.

In May 2026, [GPTZero found fabricated citations in an EY Canada report](https://gptzero.me/investigations/ey), which EY pulled. An [AICPA and CIMA survey](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/news/article/ai-transformation-opens-door-for-finance-professionals-to-build-future-ready) of 1,446 finance leaders found 88% expect AI to reshape the field more than any other trend, while only 8% feel very well prepared.

You hand your AI tool the source of truth and it assembles the report with every figure cited back to it, flagging what it can't trace. Run it as a paste-in habit before each close, a saved skill, or a triggered [agent](#tooltip-agent).

Pick one recurring report you own, then have your AI chat interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming the report, its source files, the output format, and the rule for untraceable numbers.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that creates my [monthly variance narrative / board deck / investor update] directly from my source data, so every number in the finished report is pulled from the source and cited back to it, and anything untraceable gets flagged instead of guessed. Ask me questions, one at a time, about how this should work. Cover which report to start with, where the source data lives and what format it's in, what the finished report looks like, how derived numbers (ratios, percentages, forecasts) should show their math, and what should happen when a number has no source. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) works: the interview forces the two make-or-break decisions, which report to start with and what counts as a traceable source, before any drafting happens.

items: Where your numbers actually live, and what you can hand over as one clean source file.
Whether a derived number must show its math to count as traced.
How much gets automated. A paste-in habit before each close is a complete version.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it in a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and ask where the sourcing rules are vague. Then gather access. Common [connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are your spreadsheet tool (Google Sheets, Excel), your accounting system's export or reporting [API](#tooltip-api) (QuickBooks, NetSuite), and a warehouse connector if that's where numbers live. The paste-in version needs only the source file.

**Create.** Start building the system your scope document describes, and test it on a period you've already closed and checked by hand. The prompt below is an example. Your scope document will give you a version shaped to your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Create this period's [report name] from my source data, with every number cited to its source.

Context:
- Report template or last period's version: [paste or attach]
- Source of truth: [the source spreadsheet, GL export, or system report every number should come from]

Rules:
- Every number in the output must state which row, cell, or line in the source it came from.
- If a number the template needs has no traceable match in the source, flag it explicitly. Do not guess or carry forward last period's value.
- Treat derived numbers (a percentage built from two source figures) as sourced only if you show the underlying figures and the math.
- Never adjust a source number silently. Flag discrepancies and stop. A human decides the fix.
- End with a provenance table: [Number | Source location | Status: traced / flagged].
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: building the report and the provenance table in one pass means sourcing is never a cleanup step someone skips under deadline pressure.

children.text: **Review.** Check it against the period you verified. Does every figure trace, and did it flag the number with no clean source?
**Feedback.** Fix the rule that let a miss happen, since a corrected rule fixes every cycle after it.

items: Run the same rules on a spreadsheet you inherited, before you rely on it.
Compare a deck's headline numbers against the model they summarize to catch drift.
Add a second report type that reuses the same rules.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric), not a feel check. Have your AI chat turn the scope bar into pass/fail checks and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each finished report, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks covering sourcing, derived-number math, and format. Then set up a run log I can keep next to the report, with columns for period, numbers flagged, flags that were real errors, root cause (stale source, wrong cell reference, fabricated), and what rule I changed. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the root-cause column shows after a few closes whether the weak link is the drafting, the rules, or the source data itself.

children.text: **Log** every cycle against the rubric. Note the date, which checks passed or failed, and what you changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the system passes the rubric a few cycles straight, package the prompt and your corrected rules into a reusable AI skill. A check that keeps failing is a skill candidate. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s skill-creator skill will interview you and write it, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
One durable failure mode. The system is only as good as the source file you hand it, and a number can be sourced and still stale, so keep the source export current before every run.

items: [Anthropic, Reduce hallucinations, Claude Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations) — The cite-or-retract mechanic this build applies.
[GPTZero, Investigation: Hallucinations in Ernst & Young Report](https://gptzero.me/investigations/ey) — The named incident of fabricated sourcing reaching publication.

[AICPA & CIMA, Future-Ready Finance Survey (Dec 2025)](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/news/article/ai-transformation-opens-door-for-finance-professionals-to-build-future-ready) — The 88% vs. 8% enthusiasm-vs-preparedness gap.
